name: Bat Boy: The Musical
venue: The Sarasota Players, The Crossings at Siesta Key
address: 3501 S Tamiami Trail, Suite 1130, Sarasota, FL 34239
blurb: The Sarasota Players close out the run of the cult comedy horror musical about a half boy, half bat creature found in a West Virginia cave. It is campy, loud and surprisingly tender, staged at the company's home in The Crossings at Siesta Key. Adult subject matter: recommended for ages 18 and up. Showtimes and tickets are at theplayers.org.

name: Annual Labor Day Regatta
hours_label: Racing both days from late morning · Free to watch from shore
blurb: First sailed in 1946, this is the oldest continuously held regatta in the Southeast, and it fills Sarasota Bay with hundreds of boats across five race courses. Competitors come from all over the U.S. and Canada, and roughly a thousand people turn out across the weekend. Watching from the City Island shoreline or the Ken Thompson Parkway causeway is free.

name: Exotic Cars on the Circle
blurb: Ferraris, Lamborghinis, McLarens and a rotating cast of rare supercars fill St. Armands Circle Park for the day, hosted by Ferrari Drivers SRQ. Admission is free and proceeds benefit Flight to the North Pole, which supports terminally ill children in Sarasota and Manatee counties. The shops and cafes around the Circle stay open, so it doubles as an easy Labor Day weekend morning on the island.
source: St. Armands Circle Association / City of Sarasota

name: Sarasota Farmers Market
venue: Downtown Sarasota, Lemon Ave & Main St
blurb: Every Saturday morning, Lemon Avenue and Main Street close to traffic for produce, seafood, baked goods, plants and prepared breakfast from local vendors. It is the best hour of the week to feel out downtown Sarasota on foot. Free to walk, rain or shine.
source: Sarasota Farmers Market / evergreen weekly anchor
